disorder-name.detail: Neonates with Down syndrome (Trisomy 21) confirmed postnatally by karyotype. Recruited from neonatal unit and postnatal wards at St Thomas' Hospital London (T21 study and eBiDS study).
disorder-name.supporting_text: "Neonates with a postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS were recruited from the neonatal unit and postnatal wards at St Thomas' Hospital London... data from 25 neonates with DS [12 female, 10 preterm births < 37 weeks GA, PMA at scan median (range) = 40.57 (32.43-45.57) weeks]"
disorder-name.location: FukamiGartner2023.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Participants / Neonates with DS, L61

dataset-of-origin.detail: Data were collected at a single site: Evelina Newborn Imaging Centre, St Thomas' Hospital London, under two studies: the T21 study [07/H0707/105] and the Early Brain Imaging in DS (eBiDS) study [19/LO/0667]. Neither study name appears in the normalized dataset keyword list; classified as SINGLE-SITE.
dataset-of-origin.supporting_text: "Neonates with a postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS were recruited from the neonatal unit and postnatal wards at St Thomas' Hospital London... Ethical approval was provided by London-based National Research Ethics Committees for the following studies: quantification of fetal brain development using MRI (trisomy 21 participant subgroup, henceforth denoted 'T21 study') [07/H0707/105], Early Brain Imaging in DS (eBiDS) [19/LO/0667]"
dataset-of-origin.location: FukamiGartner2023.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Ethical approval and Participants / Neonates with DS, L55-L61

age.detail: Age is reported as postmenstrual age (PMA) at scan in weeks. Only median and range are reported; mean and SD are not provided. Note: age unit is weeks (PMA), not years, per study design (neonatal cohort).
age.supporting_text: "25 neonates with DS [12 female, 10 preterm births < 37 weeks GA, PMA at scan median (range) = 40.57 (32.43-45.57) weeks]"

sex.detail: 12 females reported directly. Male N estimated as 25 - 12 = 13. Percentages calculated from counts: female 12/25 = 48.0%, male 13/25 = 52.0%. Male count is estimated; confirmed by individual-level data in Table S1 (12 F, 13 M).
